description: Orthogonal hyperedge routing connects a net of three or more ports with one tree of horizontal and vertical segments (a *rectilinear Steiner tree*). Its graph gives every vertex of the orthogonal visibility graph a horizontal and a vertical copy, joined by an edge that costs one bend. Heuristic 1 grows shortest-path trees from all ports at once and joins them with the cheapest links, as in Kruskal's method. Heuristic 2 grows and joins in turns, so later growth reuses the merged tree at no cost. A final step shifts straight runs only when that makes the tree strictly cheaper; the result is good but not proven optimal.

papers.authors: Michael Wybrow, Kim Marriott, Peter J. Stuckey
papers.title: Orthogonal Hyperedge Routing

lineage.source: connector-routing, src/hyperedge.rs: "Both heuristics of the paper run on the *separated* orthogonal visibility graph"
